page: Amazon Web Services m4.large is an entry-tier general-purpose cloud instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Running on the Xen hypervisor, it provides two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by one physical core with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.4 GHz. Cache structures include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, and FMA, whereas modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported.

The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local SSD storage is included, requiring all persistent data to reside on external block storage volumes. Similarly, there are no hardware accelerators or GPUs present, and the baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate uncached large-block read speeds of 12.28 GB/sec and write speeds of 10.68 GB/sec, reflecting the characteristics of older DDR4 memory architectures.

Benchmark metrics place the m4.large in the lower performance brackets relative to modern cloud hardware. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0 and a multi-core score of 1148.0, with stress-ng recording 1260.98 and 1666.09 respectively. Synthetic application testing demonstrates 0.75 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.85 GB/sec in static web throughput. Given its older CPU generation and constrained compute capacity, this server presents lower compute density compared to newer generations. The m4.large is suited for legacy workloads, development and staging servers, basic continuous integration tasks, and lightweight web serving where strict compute performance is not mandatory.
description: Amazon Web Services m4.large is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.4 GHz. It provides 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the Xen hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance includes support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, while lacking newer AVX-512 extensions. The server does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for disk operations. In benchmark evaluations, the m4.large registers modest computational throughput, scoring in the lower percentiles across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU suites. It yields a Redis SET throughput of 0.75 million operations per second and static web throughput of 1.85 GB/sec. The instance serves legacy deployments, lightweight background utilities, dev-test environments, and non-critical services with modest computational demands.
